verses.text: “But now people younger than me laugh at me, people whose fathers I thought weren’t fit to be put with my sheepdogs.
What good was the strength of their hands to me, when their strength had already gone?
They’re gaunt from hunger and famine. They gnaw at the dry ground in the gloom of the desolate wasteland.
They pull up salt herbs by the bushes and eat the roots of the broom tree.
People drive them out and shout after them as if they were thieves,
so they live in dreadful valleys and in holes in the ground and the rocks.
They bray among the bushes and huddle together under the nettles.
They’re children of fools, children of wicked people. They were whipped out of the land.
“Now I’m the subject of their songs. My name has become a joke to them.
They can’t stand me. They keep their distance and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.
God has loosened his cord and afflicted me, and they’ve thrown off all restraint in front of me.
The rabble rises up on my right. They knock my feet out from under me and build up paths to destroy me.
They tear up my path and push on with my destruction without anyone helping them.
They pour through as if through a wide gap in a wall, rolling in through the ruins.
Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor away like the wind, and my well-being has vanished like a cloud.
“Now my soul is pouring out inside me. Days of suffering have got hold of me.
At night my bones feel pierced, and the pain that gnaws at me never lets up.
My clothes are pulled out of shape by sheer force. They grip me like the collar of my tunic.
He’s thrown me into the mud. I’ve become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, and you don’t answer. I stand up, and you just stare at me.
You’ve turned cruel toward me. You come after me with the full strength of your hand.
You lift me into the wind and drive me along with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
I know you’ll bring me to death, to the house set aside for everyone who lives.
“Doesn’t a person stretch out a hand when they fall? Don’t they cry for help when disaster hits?
Didn’t I cry for people in trouble? Didn’t I grieve deep down for those in need?
I looked for good, and evil came. I waited for light, and darkness came.
My heart churns and won’t rest. Days of suffering have come upon me.
I go around mourning without the sun. I stand up in the gathering and cry for help.
I’m a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin turns black and peels off. My bones burn with heat.
So my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe sounds like people weeping.
